newsitem.title: USA: World Bank to lend Bosnia $90 million.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to lend Bosnia $90 million.

text.p: The World Bank said on Friday that it approved a $90 million, low-cost credit for war-torn Bosnia to help it rebuild government institutions and relaunch banking and other reforms.

The fast-disbursing loan, which will carry no interest charge and be repayable in 35 years, is designed to strengthen economic reintegration through the establishment of a new governmental structure and development of the private sector.
The Netherlands is contributing an additional $20 million to the programme.
"This credit supports a structural reform process focused on sustainability, employment creation and growth," World Bank official Christine Wallich said.
The loan brings the amount of World Bank support to Bosnia to $325 million.
The Bank, which is helping to coordinate the international drive to rebuild Bosnia, said donors have so far disbursed $405 million of the $1.8 billion in aid pledged for 1996.
"To fully finance the reconstruction programme, the sustained support of donors during the next years and the continuation of support after the elections will be critical," the World Bank said.
"A timely mobilisation of new donor pledges to finance 1997 requirements will be essential to allow reconstrucion to continue without interruption," it added.
The elections are slated to take place on Sept. 14.
The International Development Association, a World Bank affiliate, is the organisation supplying the $90 million credit.
